- allreduce/barrier: safe after receiver r's result ACK: contribution (p,r) safe iff acked[r] > p (receiver r ACKed output q=p). So E[r] = min(R[r], acked[r]).
- reduce: safe after root's result ACK: contribution (p,r) safe iff acked[root] > p. E[r] = min(R[r], acked[root]).
- broadcast: requires all three receivers: contribution (p,root) safe iff acked[d] > p for all d≠root. E[root] = min(R[root], min_{d≠root} acked[d]).
- reducescatter: requires that p's mapped receiver: contribution (p,r) safe iff acked[floor(p/(K/4))] > p mod (K/4). E[r] = max L ≤ R[r] with that property for all p<L.
- gather: requires all three receivers of that source's value at their mapped output PSNs: contribution (p,r) safe iff for all d≠r: acked[d] > 3p+ord(d,r).

Great, matches my earlier reasoning.

Note for allreduce mode 2: since E[r] = min(R[r], acked[r]) and R[r] is r's own received prefix... but note that the aggregate for input p is only complete when all four sources have contributed. But safety is per-contribution, so a partial input's contributions can still be ACKed upstream (mode 2 requires downstream ACK of the result... wait, but if input p is incomplete, no result is produced, so no result can be ACKed for p!).

Hmm. In mode 2, for allreduce: contribution (p,r) is safe after receiver r's result ACK for q=p. But receiver r can only ACK q=p if the result was sent, which requires input p complete. So in mode 2, E[r] can't exceed the complete prefix. That's automatically handled: acked[r] ≤ S[r] ≤ (complete prefix for r's outputs). So E[r] = min(R[r], acked[r]) where acked[r] ≤ number of completed inputs. Fine — no contradiction: incomplete inputs' contributions are unsafe until the input completes and the result is ACKed. ✓ That's the whole point of mode 2 (no result retransmission ownership; upstream ACK only after downstream confirmed).

For gather mode 2: same, acked[d] > 3p+ord requires the output to have been sent which requires input p complete. ✓

For reducescatter mode 2: same. ✓

For broadcast mode 2: same. ✓

OK so the formula works uniformly.

Now, incremental extension: E[r] starts at 0. try_extend(r): while E[r] < R[r] and safe(r, E[r]): E[r]++. We call try_extend after any change to R[r] or acked[]. Since safe() is monotone in time, and E[r] only increases, total work is bounded by final E[r] + number of calls. Each call does O(1) work if safe() is O(1) (O(3) for gather). Number of calls: after each R change (4 per DATA) and each acked change (4 per effective ACK). Bounded by ~8 per packet → fine.

Hmm, but careful: try_extend could be called many times when E[r] is stuck; each call costs O(1) (one safe() evaluation). Fine.

Now, one important subtlety: is `safe()` monotone? For allreduce: acked[r] > p — monotone ✓. For gather: acked[d] > 3p+ord ✓ monotone. Yes.

Now, U[r]: "The last successfully sent upstream prefix U[r] starts at zero." So U[r] = the last prefix successfully sent. When we send an ACK with prefix E[r], U[r] = E[r]. Note U[r] only increases if E[r] > U[r].

Hmm, "The last successfully sent upstream prefix U[r]" — if E[r] somehow decreased... it can't (monotone).

Now, "A retired p must be complete, have every required output acknowledged, and have U[r]>p for every required source."

- complete: all required sources present.
- every required output acknowledged: for allreduce: acked[d] > p for all d. For reduce: acked[root] > p. For broadcast: acked[d] > p for all d≠root. For barrier: acked[d] > 0 for all d (q=0). For allgather: for all d≠s: acked[d] > 3p+ord(d,s). For reducescatter: acked[floor(p/(K/4))] > p mod (K/4).
- U[r] > p for every required source.

b = longest prefix satisfying all three, i.e., b = min over p of first failing p. Incremental: maintain b, and try_advance(): while b < K and slot b is complete and outputs acked and U[r] > b for all required r: free slot b, b++.

Wait — careful: b can only advance if the slot exists and is complete. If slot b doesn't exist (no contributions at all), then it's not complete → stop.

Also, b ≤ R-ish but not necessarily related.

Total advancement ≤ K, and each attempt is O(1)-ish (for allgather, checking "every required output acknowledged" is O(3) checks... let's count: for gather, need for all d≠s (12 pairs) acked[d] > 3p+ord(d,s). That's O(12). Fine.)

Number of calls: after each change that could enable advancement: accepting a contribution (completeness), an effective ACK (acked change), a successful upstream ACK (U change). Each triggers try_advance. Each attempt costs O(small). Fine.

Now, freeing the slot when b advances: also need to free the allgather raw payloads (malloc'd). We'll manage memory carefully.

Now "occupied slots" state[1]: count of in-use slots. Note that slots are in [b, min(K,b+N)).

Hmm, wait. Is a slot allocated for every p in the window, or only for p with at least one accepted contribution? "Incomplete, completed, sent and unacknowledged records all consume the same bounded pool." — "records" = accepted contributions? Hmm, "occupied slots" — I think a slot is occupied iff at least one contribution has been accepted for that p (i.e., it holds data). A p with no data has no record. In the example, occupied=1 with one input having all 4 contributions. If we allocated slots for all p in the window regardless, then with N=1 and b=0, occupied would be 1 anyway. Not discriminating.

Let's think: "New data can occupy only logical p in [b,min(K,b+N)); data at p≥b+N is blocked... Neither can allocate or overwrite a slot." This says data allocates slots. So slots are allocated by data. So occupied = number of p in the window with ≥1 accepted contribution. ✓ And "Retired/unused storage is omitted" in the buffer digest ✓ ("Include occupied slots").

So the buffer digest only includes slots with at least one contribution.

Now, the "source mask" in the digest: bit r set for accepted contributions.

Now let's think about how the receiver's "sent prefix" S[d] interacts with retransmission and retirement.

Retirement requires all outputs ACKed: acked[d] ≥ (max q for that input)+1 for each destination d with outputs from p. And S[d] ≥ acked[d]. After retirement, slots are freed.

Now, retransmission on retry for receiver d: outputs q ∈ [acked[d], S[d]). These must have payloads available. Since retirement requires acked[d] > max q of retired inputs, all q < acked[d] are retired-or-acked. The unacknowledged ones q ∈ [acked[d], S[d]) belong to non-retired inputs (since if the input were retired, all its outputs would be acked, so q < acked[d]). So payloads are available ✓.

Wait, is that exactly right? For allgather, input p's outputs for destination d are q=3p..3p+2. If input p is retired, then for all d≠s: acked[d] > 3p+ord(d,s), i.e., acked[d] ≥ 3p+3. So all of p's outputs for d are < acked[d] ✓.

For reducescatter: input p retired requires acked[d] > q ✓.

OK good.

Now, an important question: when we retransmit, do we re-send the exact same frame (same q, same payload)? Yes, "previously sent but unacknowledged results".

Now — the retransmission must not change S[d]. ✓

Now let's think about the case where a retry happens and the retransmission encounters an output that's not available (e.g., q ≥ S[d])? We stop at S[d].

Now: "A failed result retransmission does not queue a continuation: a later retry starts again at the then-current downstream acknowledged prefix." So each retry restarts from acked[d].

Now, about the upstream ACK repeat on retry: "requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK, if any". Pending = E>U or repeat_requested, with E>0. Since the service routine already sends pending upstream ACKs first (in ascending rank), the retry's own contribution is just the retransmission part. But note: the retry also sets... hmm, does a retry set repeat_requested? "retry: rank, requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK, if any, and all of that receiver's sent/unacknowledged results". I think the retry triggers the standard service: first pending upstream ACKs for all ranks (ascending), which includes rank `rank` if pending; then the retransmission for that rank; then new results.

But here's a subtlety: if E[r] == U[r] and no repeat requested, then rank r's upstream ACK is not pending, so it's not re-sent by the generic part. Does the retry request force a repeat of the ACK even if not "pending"? "requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK, if any" — hmm. "if any" suggests: if there is an eligible ACK (E[r] > 0), repeat it. But that conflicts with "Pending upstream ACK means E>U or a repeat was requested, with E>0."

Hmm. Let's think about it more carefully. The retry event "requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK, if any, and all of that receiver's sent/unacknowledged results, with the priority above". I think "with the priority above" means the ordering is as described. The pending condition defines what gets emitted. If we interpret the retry as setting repeat_requested[rank] = true, then the ACK would be sent if E>0 (consistent with "if any"), and then the retransmission. Hmm, that's a plausible reading too: "requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK" = sets the repeat request.

Which is right? The difference matters when E[r] == U[r] > 0 and no repeat was requested: does the retry send an ACK?

Consider the design intent: `retry` is a way to test retransmission behavior. The natural reading of "requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK, if any" is that the retry asks for the ACK to be (re)sent if there's an eligible one. But then "Pending upstream ACK means E>U or a repeat was requested, with E>0" would be the general rule and the retry would set the repeat flag.

Hmm, "A repeat request persists until an ACK succeeds" — if the retry sets repeat_requested and the ACK send fails, the request persists, so a later flush would retry it. That's consistent.

If instead the retry merely triggers the standard service (which sends ACKs only when pending), then "requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK, if any" would be a no-op in the E==U case, which makes the phrase "if any" strange (it'd be "if pending").

I lean toward: retry sets repeat_requested[rank] = true (requesting a repeat of its eligible ACK if E>0), then runs the service with the retransmission step enabled for that rank.
